title: A moving clock ticks slower by $(c - v)/c$

statements.text: For a moving source to measure the speed of its own light as $c$, with its measuring lengths unchanged, its clock must tick slower by the factor $(c - v)/c$: an absolute interval $\Delta t$ registers as $\Delta\tau = \Delta t (c - v)/c$. The model ties this slowdown to inertia, in an account still to be published.

sources.quote: Assuming unchanged measuring lengths, its clock would have to tick more slowly by the factor (c − v)/c.
Within my model, this clock slowdown is connected to inertia.
